name: Subnet 0
whatItDoes: Root subnet: Bittensor's TAO transport and stake/validator relay layer — holders stake to root validators and move stake between subnets through it. It is not a mining protocol.
whatMinerDoes: Nothing in the mining sense — subnet 0 is the root network for stake transport and validator relay; its registered slots support stake/relay mechanics rather than service work, and the large 'miner emission' figure reflects staking mechanics, not rewards for a task protocol.
whatValidatorDoes: Root validators anchor the network and relay stake/emission between subnets rather than scoring a mining service.
rewardBasis: n/a — stake transport, not a mining protocol

name: Apex
whatItDoes: Macrocosmos's 'general intelligence platform': anyone can bring a problem, a global network of miners competes to solve it, and Apex routes the best solution back. Positioned as a decentralized orchestration layer for intelligence at scale.
whatMinerDoes: Miners compete to solve problems/submissions routed to them, using agentic mining stacks — the repo recommends AGENTS.md as the guide for agentic mining and points to the Apex CLI for miner setup. The extract's README is light on hardware specifics, so exact GPU/API requirements are not documented here; incentive comes from validators continuously scoring submissions.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators continuously score miner submissions and distribute rewards accordingly.
rewardBasis: continuous scoring of solution submissions

name: DSperse
whatItDoes: Verifiable and distributed inference on Bittensor: miners run AI model inferences that have been converted into zero-knowledge circuits, so outputs come with cryptographic proof they were computed faithfully.
whatMinerDoes: Miners receive input data from validators, run verifiable inference with custom models converted into ZK circuits, and return the output together with a zero-knowledge proof of inference to the requesting validator. The README does not specify hardware; the work is inference plus proof generation.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators produce input data, distribute verified-inference requests, check each returned ZK proof for authenticity, and score miners on metrics like proof size and response time.
rewardBasis: proof validity + proof size + response time

name: Teutonic
whatItDoes: King-of-the-hill pretraining competition: miners submit model checkpoints and a successful challenger dethrones the current 'king' model to take the subnet's emission share.
whatMinerDoes: Miners train language-model checkpoints and submit one immutable checkpoint per hotkey (an Ed25519 hotkey is required because the validator encrypts temporary upload credentials to it). Each submission is verified and raced against the current king in a remote GPU evaluator using paired cross-entropy scoring; a challenger that beats the king becomes the new king. This is real GPU training work with winner-take-most economics.
whatValidatorDoes: The validator verifies each submission, sends challenger and current king to a remote GPU evaluator for paired cross-entropy scoring, updates subnet weights, and publishes the resulting state.
rewardBasis: paired cross-entropy score vs current king (king-of-the-hill)

name: Targon
whatItDoes: AI infrastructure platform secured end-to-end by Trusted Execution Environments and confidential compute; on-chain it is described as an incentivized compute marketplace powered by the Targon Virtual Machine (TVM).
whatMinerDoes: The extract's README contains no miner section — only the TEE/confidential-compute platform pitch and a hosting note about NVIDIA Confidential Compute integration. Miners are understood to provision TVM-compatible confidential compute capacity, but concrete hardware requirements, query flow, and scoring are not documented in this file, so treat specifics as unverified.
whatValidatorDoes: Not documented in the extract (README covers the platform/TEE pitch only).
rewardBasis: not documented in extract

name: Hone
whatItDoes: RLVR (reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards) on Bittensor: coding challenges are leased and dealt to serving miners, whose solutions are graded against hidden tests to produce verifiable training/reward signal.
whatMinerDoes: Miners serve an LLM-backed coder: validators lease a public coding challenge and rotation-deal it to half of the serving miners; the miner's model produces a solution response that is committed, then graded when the validator reveals the hidden tests. The repo ships only a small GLM-5.2-API-backed demo miner as a protocol reference (miners need their own model-provider key), so production miners supply their own model backend; specifics of production miner hardware are not documented in the extract.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators lease coding challenges, deal them to half the serving miners, commit signed responses, reveal hidden tests, grade every response in a local Docker sandbox (up to 16 one-CPU grading containers), and set weights.
rewardBasis: hidden-test pass rate, Docker-graded

name: Numinous
whatItDoes: Forecasting protocol aiming to aggregate agents into superhuman LLM forecasters: instead of scoring individual predictions, the subnet scores the underlying agentic models that produce them.
whatMinerDoes: Miners develop and deploy forecasting agents (code) that compete for the daily reward pool. Agents run in validator-operated sandboxes with access to inference (reasoning models), tools (e.g., news providers), and context (historical data, baseline reasoning); execution limits, memory rules, and penalties apply per the subnet rules. Agent execution and code are fully visible to the protocol, and best agents become building blocks for meta-models and prediction-market resolution.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators run the physical infrastructure that executes and scores the forecasting agents inside tool-accessible sandboxes.
rewardBasis: agent forecast accuracy in sandbox evaluations (daily pool)

name: Allways
whatItDoes: Settlement layer for agents and applications: native cross-chain transactions for programs that hold one asset and need to pay in another — no wrapped tokens, no bridges, no custodian (SOL and TAO hubs paired against BTC, ETH, USDC variants, and more).
whatMinerDoes: Miners run the reference settlement software (alw CLI): they deposit collateral (SOL locally or TAO into the Bittensor vault), bind their hotkey, get voted active by validators, and post quotes (rates) for cross-chain pairs; when routed, they complete the native swap legs. The README explicitly flags the miner as reference software to be reviewed and hardened before running. minerWorkType in practice is on-chain operations and liquidity provision rather than ML compute.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators independently verify both legs of each swap on-chain, vote on miner activation, and a smart contract enforces outcomes through collateral and slashing.
rewardBasis: verified cross-chain swap completion + quoted rates

name: Vanta
whatItDoes: Formerly Proprietary Trading Network: a decentralized liquidity and execution engine for prop firms and traders where miners submit trade signals that are tracked as live portfolios.
whatMinerDoes: Miners produce and send trade signals to validators (the extract's README has no explicit miner section beyond the Bittensor primer, so signal format, strategies, and hardware are not documented in detail). Signals are validated, stored, and tracked over time as portfolio returns, which drive miner incentive.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators receive trade signals from miners, ensure the trades are valid, store them, and track portfolio returns.
rewardBasis: tracked portfolio returns of submitted trades

name: iota
whatItDoes: Incentivized Orchestrated Training Architecture: pretrains large language models across a network of heterogeneous, unreliable, permissionless, token-incentivized machines using data- and pipeline-parallelism to lower hardware requirements.
whatMinerDoes: Miners run GPU workers that the orchestrator stitches into a training pipeline: model layers are distributed across heterogeneous miners and activations are streamed between them (shared S3 bucket holds activations and layer weights). Miners compete to process as many activations as possible in the training stage, periodically upload local weights, and merge activations via a Butterfly All-Reduce variant. Starting is `bash ./start_miner.sh` with PM2 support; validators spot-check that work was performed as required.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators spot-check miners to ensure training work (activation processing) was performed as required.
rewardBasis: activations processed, spot-check verified

name: Pareton
whatItDoes: Runs inference-optimization campaigns: miners submit code patches that make pinned vLLM/SGLang serving baselines faster, and every validated improvement becomes the new floor for the next campaign.
whatMinerDoes: Miners author git patches against a campaign-pinned baseline (vLLM or SGLang; example campaign targets Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 on four RTX 5090s with 262K context), upload via presigned S3, and commit campaign_id/baseline_commit/patch_hash on-chain. Patches pass identity/integrity/base-apply/surface validation gates, are built hermetically inside the pinned base image, and are benchmarked head-to-head against the baseline and current leader on a sampled prompt set; the best image takes the crown for that round.
whatValidatorDoes: Pareton's watcher/worker pipeline validates patch integrity and allowed changes, builds patches in a reproducible container environment, and benchmarks real performance gains per round (on-chain scoring still design-only).
rewardBasis: benchmarked performance gains vs pinned baseline (per round)

name: TrajectoryRL
whatItDoes: Agentic RL as a service: optimizes agent trajectories to make agents cheaper, safer, and more reliable. In the live Season 2, miners compete on fusion policies that decide which open-weight models answer an agent request, and the winning policy is served as a product (Engy's engy/auto mode).
whatMinerDoes: Miners submit fusion policies — programs that decide, per request, which open-weight models on the Engy platform answer an agent and in what combination. Validators evaluate every submission in real sandboxes against tasks with hidden tests (example eval packs: git-leak-recovery, postgres-csv-clean, using the exact validator code with an Engy API key); the best submission holds the seat until a better one takes it. The extract details the validator/test workflow more than the miner stack.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators evaluate every submission in real sandboxes against hidden-test tasks with stake-weighted consensus; the seated fusion policy is served as engy/auto.
rewardBasis: hidden-test sandbox evaluation, stake-weighted (seat held until beaten)

name: Compute Horde
whatItDoes: Turns untrusted miner GPUs into trusted, scalable compute for other subnets' validators — a decentralized GPU job-execution layer meant to help Bittensor scale beyond its current limits.
whatMinerDoes: Miners accept job requests from validators and manage executors (Docker-based) that perform GPU tasks and return results; a one-command installer provisions an Ubuntu server as a miner. To maximize earnings miners stake collateral with validators (unlocking paid organic jobs), preload likely Docker job images to cut latency, and optionally run a DDoS shield to stay online. Scoring explicitly incentivizes completing organic tasks, with collateral creating economic pressure to behave honestly.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators receive organic requests via the Facilitator, distribute tasks to miners, and cross-validate results with a dedicated Trusted Miner (A6000) that pre-runs part of the validation tasks; optional collateral-contract integration filters miners and enables slashing.
rewardBasis: completed organic jobs (cross-validated by trusted miner)

name: Data Universe
whatItDoes: Macrocosmos's data-scraping and sentiment subnet: collects real-time data from X (Twitter), Reddit, and YouTube transcripts into what it bills as the world's largest open-source social media dataset, queryable for other subnets and businesses.
whatMinerDoes: Miners run scrapers for a defined set of DataSources and store the scraped DataEntities (webpages, posts, transcripts, prices) in their own database, organized into buckets by source, time, and type — data lives across miners rather than a central store. Validators periodically sample each miner's MinerIndex to verify correctness and track a credibility factor that scales the miner's score, so misrepresenting what data you hold is always penalized. Miners must follow Macrocosmos's data-compliance policy (UK GDPR awareness, prohibited content).
whatValidatorDoes: Validators sample data from each miner's index to verify correctness, maintain a credibility score, and use it to scale miner rewards.
rewardBasis: data volume × correctness, credibility-scaled

name: Cacheon
whatItDoes: An inference-throughput competition built around SGLang: miners submit GPU-kernel contributions that must speed up a validator-owned model without hurting output quality.
whatMinerDoes: Miners submit inspectable GPU-kernel contributions at registered boundaries in a validator-owned model, using the miner SDK and examples shipped in the repo. Contributions are admitted through a typed, isolated pipeline and are only rewarded if the improvement reproduces under the registered throughput and quality policy. The README flags Cacheon as pre-release software, so implemented paths and production readiness are separate claims.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators admit kernel contributions through a typed, isolated evaluation pipeline and reward only improvements that reproduce under the registered throughput and quality policy.
rewardBasis: reproducible throughput gains under quality policy

name: ORO
whatItDoes: Evaluates AI shopping agents on real-world commerce tasks: miners submit agents that search products, compare prices, and make purchase decisions, benchmarked against ShoppingBench (2.5 million real products).
whatMinerDoes: Miners write Python agents defining an `agent_main(problem_data)` function: the validator injects a per-task environment object, and the agent drives the shopping session by calling runtime-supplied tools (binding, policy_view.tools) until the environment reports done. A reference implementation (src/agent/environment_agent.py) and Docker-based local testing are provided. The best agent holds the leaderboard top spot and earns emissions proportional to validator stake; challengers must beat a decaying score threshold to take the crown.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators run each agent in an isolated Docker sandbox against the ShoppingBench problem suite, scoring ground-truth accuracy, format compliance, and field matching.
rewardBasis: ShoppingBench task accuracy + format compliance (decaying leader threshold)

name: kenju
whatItDoes: Undocumented subnet: no on-chain description ('0x'), no GitHub repo, and only generic Bittensor boilerplate in web results; a small live emission (14.57 TAO/day, 1 rewarded miner of 18 registered) suggests minimal activity.
whatMinerDoes: Unknown — no repo or on-chain description exists and the web-search snippets returned are generic Bittensor/extractor-page text, so what the 18 registered miners actually do cannot be determined from available evidence.
whatValidatorDoes: Nothing documented — no description or repo exists for this subnet.
rewardBasis: unknown — no documented incentive mechanism

name: 404—GEN
whatItDoes: A decentralized 3D content generation competition: miners submit open-source solutions for AI-powered 3D model generation and validators run transparent per-round competitions to find the best.
whatMinerDoes: Miners submit open-source 3D-generation solutions each competition round (submission locations are recorded per hotkey in per-round state). The validator side regenerates outputs from submissions for verification and runs judge/duel matches with per-prompt outcomes, so miners compete on generation quality rather than serving latency. The extract's README is brief; concrete model/hardware requirements for miners are not documented here.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators collect submissions, regenerate outputs for verification, and run judge-service duels with per-prompt match reports to determine the best solution.
rewardBasis: head-to-head duel outcomes on 3D generation quality

name: Zeus
whatItDoes: Decentralized weather/environmental forecasting (Orpheus AI): miners compete to produce the best forecasts on the full Earth grid for variables used heavily in energy trading, scored against the EU Copernicus ERA5 reanalysis dataset.
whatMinerDoes: Miners run forecasting models that answer global ERA5 challenges issued by validators for four surface variables — 2 m temperature, 100 m wind u- and v-components, and surface solar radiation downwards — producing forecasts over the full Earth grid. Forecasts are scored as reveals against ERA5 reanalysis data, so this is real ML weather-model work (training/inference on geospatial data); the extract's README describes the challenge format but not miner hardware specifics.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators issue global ERA5 forecasting challenges, score revealed forecasts against ERA5 reanalysis, keep rank history, and set subnet weights from verified performance.
rewardBasis: forecast accuracy vs ERA5 reanalysis (rank history)

name: blockmachine
whatItDoes: Decentralized RPC and archive-node infrastructure for Bittensor and Ethereum: independent miners compete to serve node requests with every response integrity-checked before it reaches the caller.
whatMinerDoes: Miners operate RPC/archive nodes for Bittensor and Ethereum and compete to serve requests; every response is checked with Merkle proofs before delivery, so miners must serve authentic chain data rather than just low latency. The extract's README is short — hardware requirements and the detailed scoring formula are not documented here.
whatValidatorDoes: Responses are verified with Merkle proofs before reaching callers (proof-based verification; validator-side scoring details are not in the extract).
rewardBasis: Merkle-proof-verified RPC serving

name: Witness
whatItDoes: Video-understanding subnet ('Understand video. Not just watch it.'): miners turn video clips into structured event descriptions, producing a decentralized video-analysis service. Note: a temporary policy dated September 15, 2026 puts the subnet in 100% burn — miner rewards are paused.
whatMinerDoes: Miners receive video clips from validators and return structured events (an MP4 protocol/integration doc covers production v5.2), i.e., video-understanding inference work. Important for operators: under the temporary 100%-burn policy (September 15, 2026) miner rewards are paused and validators are instructed to apply the burn update, so there is currently no incentive to point hardware here until reverted.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators compare miners' returned structured events against private human annotations and rank eligible miners.
rewardBasis: agreement with private human annotations (currently 100% burn — rewards paused)

name: AdTAO
whatItDoes: A verifiable prediction market for Google Ads campaign outcomes: miners' models predict distributions of future campaign deltas, and settled real-world outcomes drive emissions.
whatMinerDoes: Miners build a digest-pinned Docker container that reads ad-account episodes as NDJSON on stdin and writes P10/P50/P90 predictions over 7-, 14-, and 28-day campaign deltas as NDJSON on stdout; they register once, push the container, and commit its digest on-chain. The subnet itself pulls, gate-admits, and runs the container every day against a fresh basket of real account changes — miners do NOT POST daily predictions. Reference baseline runs on CPU (2 cores/4 GB minimum, GPU optional for heavier models).
whatValidatorDoes: Validators/settle clock score matured (episode × horizon) rows into each miner's standing, map standings through the published weight curve, and set weights on chain; public receipts let any miner reproduce a day's score.
rewardBasis: prediction calibration vs settled outcomes (weight curve)

name: Desearch
whatItDoes: The subnet behind Desearch's decentralized real-time intelligence layer: coordinates miners that serve live web, X/Twitter, and multi-source search data for the Desearch API and console products.
whatMinerDoes: Miners run axons that serve live web, X/Twitter, and multi-source search data (search links/results) requested through the validator's FastAPI service, which powers Desearch products. The extract's README stops short of miner internals — hardware, scraping stack, and exact query cadence are not documented here, so treat implementation details as unverified.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators run a FastAPI service exposing search-link routes (web, Twitter, combined) that query miner axons and score the returned results.
rewardBasis: validator-scored search result quality

name: Trishool
whatItDoes: An AI-alignment subnet building a state-of-the-art AI guard model: miners contribute adversarial prompts, and evaluated results aggregate into on-chain weights.
whatMinerDoes: Miners submit adversarial prompts targeting the subnet's guard-model evaluation fixtures (the eval harness uses rotating synthetic values and PII corpora reachable only via dedicated eval plugin tools). Validators evaluate submissions via agent tooling (OpenClaw + Judge) and aggregate scores on-chain. The extract documents the validator/eval harness in more depth than the miner stack, so miner hardware and tooling specifics are not detailed here.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators evaluate submitted adversarial prompts via agents (OpenClaw + Judge), aggregate the scores, and write them as on-chain weights.
rewardBasis: agent-judged adversarial prompt scores

name: Quasar
whatItDoes: Production training system for continuing pretraining of the Quasar Preview MoE model on Bittensor, with a stated goal of 10T+ additional pretraining tokens through a verifiable decentralized run.
whatMinerDoes: Miners claim signed training leases on fragments of the model (the orchestrator splits Quasar Preview's trainable tensors into 24 fragments) and train them on their own GPUs — multi-GPU is supported via QUASAR_MINER_DEVICES — submitting signed live fragment claims and live-control grants as they work. Validator-approved live fragments are merged by the orchestrator, and periodic updated Quasar checkpoints are released. Emission follows accepted live merge events, so unverified work earns nothing.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators validate assigned training work, write verdicts, summarize accepted live merge events, and set weights from them (validators do not merge model updates themselves).
rewardBasis: accepted live fragment merges (validator-approved training work)

name: UR
whatItDoes: A peer-to-peer privacy network and encryption layer for the internet: network operators run servers, independent providers carry ingress/egress traffic (VPN-style), and validators prove real-time transit through provider chains.
whatMinerDoes: Miners act as bandwidth providers in two tiers inside one mechanism: a pool tier (on-ramp; providers join via a network operator's vault-owned pool UID and are paid by Merkle claim based on implied usage × quality) and a top-level tier where the ~200 fleets with the most split-adjusted distinct routable egress-IP counts claim their own miner UID and are paid natively. Providers graduate between tiers as routable-IP breadth changes — supply breadth, not traffic volume, is the headline metric. No ML compute involved; this is bandwidth/exit-node provisioning.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators run the routing-verification protocol — walking server-assigned chains of providers to prove real-time transit and measure which providers are weakest links — then score both tiers each 7-day epoch under commit-reveal.
rewardBasis: verified routing quality × routable egress-IP breadth

name: Perturb
whatItDoes: A decentralized adversarial-robustness network: miners attack production-grade image classifiers with imperceptible perturbations, producing an adversarial training dataset and on-chain robustness certificates (relevant to EU AI Act conformity).
whatMinerDoes: Miners poll the task API for the current task, run baseline PGD-style attacks to craft perturbed images that flip a fixed EfficientNetV2-L classifier on ImageNet-1k images, and upload/submit the perturbed image URL; they can also fine-tune and submit their own EfficientNetV2-L model daily (training/train.py, training/submit.py). Minimum box is 4 vCPU/16 GB RAM with an 8+ GB-VRAM GPU recommended; miners serve no axon — the validator handles all verification and scoring.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators construct challenges from real ImageNet images, mathematically verify every submitted adversarial image (prediction flip + perturbation norm), run daily model evaluations to pick a winner, and set weights per epoch from cross-validator consensus.
rewardBasis: verified adversarial-attack success + daily model-eval winner

name: Orion
whatItDoes: A data-mining subnet: campaigns define the data a model needs, miners turn assigned source data into model-ready datasets, and validators reward only verified submissions (first consumer: the Quasar model).
whatMinerDoes: Miners receive signed campaign assignments (current campaign covers coding, mathematics, technical data, and general knowledge) and process real batches of source data into model-ready dataset snapshots, using a campaign-pinned hosted judge plus a locally-run silx-ai/Quasar-Preview model on the miner GPU, then upload one signed dataset snapshot to scoped storage. The miner command uses `--devices 0` (GPU) and a Chutes API key for the judge.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators validate submitted work and independently replay a hidden sample before calculating rewards and setting Bittensor weights.
rewardBasis: verified dataset quality (hidden-sample replay)

name: SayGM
whatItDoes: gm: a drop-in LLM API gateway for Claude, GPT, and Gemini — buyers point existing OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini SDKs at the gateway and get identical behavior, while miners supply upstream API capacity and earn the spread. The gateway runs inside Intel TDX TEEs so neither operators nor hosts see buyer content or miners' upstream keys.
whatMinerDoes: Miners deploy the gm-published miner image on their own funded Phala Cloud account (CVM with Intel TDX) via the gmcli tool — no local Docker build needed by default. They bring their own upstream provider API keys (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Chutes, Z.ai, Moonshot, DeepInfra, KubeTEE, Engy, Moonmath, NEAR AI Cloud, or Bedrock/Foundry/Azure transports) and serve buyer traffic through the attested TEE data plane, earning the margin between buyer price and upstream cost. This is API-relay work, not local GPU inference.
whatValidatorDoes: Not documented in the extract — the README covers the miner/operator side (image, CLI, deployment); scoring of gateway workers is not described.
rewardBasis: served gateway requests (spread over upstream API cost)

name: hotfloat
whatItDoes: Inference-optimization competition ('Fastest server wins'): miners submit containerized LLM inference servers and the fastest correct one takes most of the emission. Note: the repo README carries the Cacheon SN14 branding (links to cacheon.ai and tao.app/subnets/14) — it appears to be the same competition lineage rebranded/migrated to SN29, matching the on-chain 'Inference optimization' description.
whatMinerDoes: Miners build an inference server that serves Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct via /v1/chat/completions with streaming and logprobs, package it as a Docker image (max 20 GB; model weights are mounted at runtime, not baked in), push it to a public registry, then pay the submission fee and commit the image digest on-chain. Validators run it on an 8-GPU TP=8 pod (8x H200/B200/B300 Tier A, 8x H100 fallback), so GPU hardware is only needed for local testing — the competition is won by serving-software optimization.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators scan the chain for new commitments, pull the image, run it with weights mounted, and score end-to-end response-time improvement over the pinned vLLM baseline — but only after a greedy-decoding correctness gate (fail = zero score); winner takes 80% of the pool, runner-up 20%, with a 1% beat margin to prevent churn.
rewardBasis: end-to-end response time vs vLLM baseline, correctness-gated (80/20 split)

name: Endure Network
whatItDoes: A decentralized risk-intelligence network (launched June 2026): Bittensor miners act as competing risk analysts whose predictions are scored over time for accuracy; research mentions it will power 'Forge', a forthcoming TAO-native product.
whatMinerDoes: Based on web research only: miners operate as competing risk analysts producing risk predictions/assessments, scored over time on how accurately their predictions play out. No repo is published on-chain (on-chain GitHub is empty), so hardware requirements, query cadence, and software stack are unknown — flagging this as research-grade information rather than README-verified.
whatValidatorDoes: Not documented in available research; miners are scored over time on the accuracy of their risk predictions.
rewardBasis: risk-prediction accuracy over time

name: rec4ll
whatItDoes: Recall: decentralized retrieval-augmented generation for Bittensor — an open competition that discovers the best RAG pipelines and routes user queries to the top performers, described as an always-improving, community-owned search engine with citations.
whatMinerDoes: Per the (unusually detailed) on-chain description, miners serve embedding models, vector search, and LLM inference as complete RAG pipelines answering user queries. No repo is published on-chain (on-chain GitHub is empty) and web results merely repeat the listing text, so concrete stacks, hardware sizing, and query protocols are not documented — GPU inference serving is implied by the work described.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators independently evaluate retrieval accuracy and answer quality of miners' RAG pipelines.
rewardBasis: retrieval accuracy + answer quality

name: ItsAI
whatItDoes: AI-generated-text detection (It's AI): classifies whether text was human-written or AI-generated, with a deep-scan mode showing per-sentence AI probabilities; the on-chain description claims top accuracy on the MGTD benchmark.
whatMinerDoes: The extract's README has no miner section — it describes the product (detection + deep scan) rather than the mining protocol. By the subnet's shape, miners are understood to serve AI-detection model inference when queried by validators, but hardware, model, and query cadence are not documented in this file, so treat specifics as unverified. Emission is broadly spread: 235 of 256 miners currently earn.
whatValidatorDoes: Not documented in the extract.
rewardBasis: not documented in extract

name: ReadyAI
whatItDoes: ReadyAI (Conversation Genome Project): a low-cost, resource-minimal data-structuring and semantic-tagging pipeline that turns raw conversation data into structured data for vector databases and AI applications.
whatMinerDoes: Miners run a standard axon neuron (python neurons.miner; Docker/PM2/RunPod guides provided, axon port must be publicly reachable) and receive conversation batches from validators, which they annotate into structured/semantically tagged outputs using LLM backends — the design diagram shows miners wired to OpenAI GPT, Anthropic Claude, or local LLM APIs. This is API-annotation work rather than local GPU training; 244 of 256 miners currently earn, so emission is broadly spread.
whatValidatorDoes: Validators retrieve conversations (by default via the ReadyAI conversation-server API, with a custom-datastore option) and send them to miners, scoring the returned structured annotations.
rewardBasis: structured-annotation quality on conversation batches
